content:
maria: Heads-up: on canary after last deploy I'm seeing heavy dash open times in EU. Trace dump attached: https://redwood/trace/1761223344.png

sam: Repro'd. Opening dashboard with ~200 series causes main-thread parse spike ~350ms and JS GC bursts. LCP +1.1s vs baseline.

kevin: Collected client-net logs: multiple prefetches are returning 204 and a couple 503s from our CDN edge. Prefetch->retry seems to refill network queue and delays chunk eval. Snippet: `GET /static/chunks/vendor-85.prefetch.js -> 204` repeated.

anya: Two knobs to try now: 1) revert the routing weight increase for EU (recent change in rollout policy concentrated clients on smaller KV pool), 2) disable prefetch for large shared chunks on canary and lazy-load telemetry.

maria: If prefetch fails and we still parse a big combined bundle, telemetry eager init (imported at module top-level) grabs the main thread and amplifies the stall. Moving telemetry init to requestIdleCallback or import() should help.

sam: Agreed. Short-term mitigation steps: flip `console.routing.eu_weight` back to 0.6 and set `feature.console.prefetch_mode=off` for the canary group. Also set `feature.telemetry.lazy_init=true`. Can we do a 2% canary first?

kevin: 2% sounds safer. I can run a quick staging test: reduced weight -> prefetch collisions drop ~40% in our simulator.

anya: I'll stage a config patch now and target a tiny canary cohort. Patch id cfg-1761223352. Applying in 20s. If unstable we abort and rollback the config.

deploy-bot: config update queued: cfg-1761223352. Target: canary(eu:2%). ETA apply: 20s.

maria: Running automated perf sweep after apply. Metrics I'm watching: LCP, First CPU Idle, bundle-parse time, number of prefetch 204/503 responses.

sam: If we see parse time drop and 204s disappear we hold for 6h and then plan a non-urgent proper fix (split vendor chunk, move telemetry out of main). If not, rollback and investigate CDN edge.

kevin: FYI I also saw one client sample where `Cache-Control` mismatch caused prefetch to return 204 even though chunk exists. Might be a CDN header edge-case introduced by asset pipeline change. Will open follow-up issue.

anya: I'll post the hotfix status here. If someone spots downstream dashboards still slow, tag @anya and paste chrome://tracing snippet or HAR. :rocket:
